}}'''Jean-Marie Tarascon''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry|FRSC]] (born September 21, 1953) is [[professor]] of chemistry at the [[Collège de France]] in [[Paris]] and director of the French Research Network on [[Electrochemistry|Electrochemical]] [[Energy storage|Energy Storage]] (RS2E).<ref>[http://www.energie-rs2e.com/en RS2E Research network on electrochemical energy storage], energie-rs2e.com</ref><ref name=googlescholar>{{GoogleScholar|TF03-1UAAAAJ}}</ref><ref name=scopus>{{Scopus|id=35416421800}}</ref>

==Education==
Tarascon was educated at the [[University of Bordeaux]], where he was awarded a [[Diplôme d'études universitaires générales]] in [[physics]] and [[chemistry]], a [[Master of Science]] degree in [[chemical engineering]], and a [[PhD]] in [[solid-state chemistry]] in 1981.<ref name=cv/><ref name=eni/>

==Career==
Following his PhD, Tarascon did [[postdoctoral research]] at [[Cornell University]].<ref name=cornell>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1021/ic00134a047| title = Ambivalent behavior of ytterbium in the ytterbium molybdenum sulfide YbMo<sub>6</sub>S<sub>8</sub>-ytterbium molybdenum selenide YbMo<sub>6</sub>Se<sub>8</sub> pseudobinary system| journal = Inorganic Chemistry| volume = 21| issue = 4| pages = 1505| year = 1982| last1 = Tarascon | first1 = J. M. | last2 = Johnson | first2 = D. C. | last3 = Sienko | first3 = M. J.}}</ref> He worked at [[Bell Labs]]<ref name=bellabs1>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevB.28.6397| title = Preparation and chemical and physical properties of the new layered phases Li<sub>x</sub>Ti<sub>1−y</sub>M<sub>y</sub>S<sub>2</sub> with M=V,Cr,or ''Fe''| journal = Physical Review B| volume = 28| issue = 11| pages = 6397| year = 1983| last1 = Tarascon | first1 = J.| last2 = Disalvo | first2 = F.| last3 = Eibschutz | first3 = M.| last4 = Murphy | first4 = D.| last5 = Waszczak | first5 = J.| bibcode=1983PhRvB..28.6397T }}</ref><ref name=bellabs2>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevB.29.172| title = New superconducting ternary molybdenum chalcogenides InMo<sub>6</sub>Se<sub>8</sub>,T1Mo<sub>6</sub>S<sub>8</sub>, and T1Mo<sub>6</sub>Se<sub>8</sub>| journal = Physical Review B| volume = 29| pages = 172–180| year = 1984| last1 = Tarascon | first1 = J.| last2 = Disalvo | first2 = F.| last3 = Murphy | first3 = D.| last4 = Hull | first4 = G.| last5 = Waszczak | first5 = J.| issue = 1| bibcode = 1984PhRvB..29..172T}}</ref> and [[Telcordia Technologies|Bellcore]]<ref name=bellcore/> from 1982 to 1994, then moved to the [[University of Picardie Jules Verne]] in 1994. He has been at the College de France since 2010. He is also credited with laying foundations of the reputable Erasmus mundus masters course in energy storage and conversion "Materials for energy storage and conversion" hosted by UPJV, Amiens in association with seven universities across the globe and several energy research networks.

==Research==
Tarascon's research<ref>{{YouTube|id=MXjOFW1cKnw|title=Jean-Marie Tarascon: Electrochemical Energy Conversion and Storage}}, [[Hong Kong University of Science and Technology]] 2014-04-24</ref> investigates the synthesis of novel electronic phenomena and materials such as [[Superconductivity|superconductors]], [[Ferroelectricity|ferroelectrics]], [[fluoride glass]]es, [[Rechargeable battery|rechargeable batteries]]<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1038/35104644| pmid = 11713543| title = Issues and challenges facing rechargeable lithium batteries| year = 2001| last1 = Tarascon | first1 = J.M. | journal = Nature| volume = 414| issue = 6861| pages = 359–67| last2 = Armand | first2 = M. | bibcode = 2001Natur.414..359T| s2cid = 2468398}}</ref> and [[colossal magnetoresistance]].<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1016/S1359-0286(99)80003-5| title = Electronic materials| journal = Current Opinion in Solid State and Materials Science| volume = 4| pages = 3–4| year = 1999| last1 = Tarascon | first1 = J. M. | last2 = Chaudhari | first2 = P. | issue = 1| bibcode = 1999COSSM...4....3T }}</ref> He has made many contributions to superconductivity and was the original proponent of the thin and [[Lithium polymer battery|flexible plastic lithium ion battery]].<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1038/35035045| pmid = 11028997| year = 2000| last1 = Tarascon | first1 = J. M. | title = Nano-sized transition-metal oxides as negative-electrode materials for lithium-ion batteries| journal = Nature| volume = 407| issue = 6803| pages = 496–9| last2 = Poizot | first2 = P.| last3 = Laruelle | first3 = S.| last4 = Grugeon | first4 = S.| last5 = Dupont | first5 = L. | bibcode = 2000Natur.407..496P| s2cid = 205009092}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | pmid = 18338357| year = 2008| last1 = Bruce| first1 = P. G.| title = Nanomaterials for rechargeable lithium batteries| journal = Angewandte Chemie International Edition| volume = 47| issue = 16| pages = 2930–46| last2 = Scrosati| first2 = B| last3 = Tarascon| first3 = J. M.| doi = 10.1002/anie.200702505}}</ref><ref>Materials for Sustainable Energy {{ISBN|9814317640}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Tarascon was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society|Foreign Member of the Royal Society (ForMemRS)]] in 2014. His nomination reads:<ref name=royal>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/fellowship/2014/jean-marie-tarascon/ |title=Professor Jean-Marie Tarascon ForMemRS |publisher=The Royal Society |archive-date=2014-05-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140502071611/https://royalsociety.org/people/fellowship/2014/jean-marie-tarascon/ |location=London |url-status=dead }}</ref>

{{quote|Jean-Marie Tarascon is distinguished for his outstanding leadership in the [[Materials science|materials chemistry]] of [[Energy transformation|energy conversion]] and storage devices and for seminal studies of [[High-temperature superconductivity|high temperature superconductors]]. His pioneering work on electrode reaction processes that can store more energy than those in [[Lithium-ion battery|conventional lithium-ion batteries]], his work on [[Molecular electronics|molecular electrodes]] and his realization of the plastic battery, have changed thinking in the field.}}

Tarascon was honoured by the [[New Jersey Inventors Hall of Fame]] in 2002.<ref>[http://www.njinvent.org/awards/Awards2002.html New Jersey Inventors 2002 Award Winners Hall of Fame] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141222002259/http://www.njinvent.org/awards/Awards2002.html |date=2014-12-22 }}, New Jersey Inventors</ref> He was nominated to the [[French Academy of Sciences|Académie des Sciences]] in 2005, and was the [[University of Picardie Jules Verne|University of Picardie Jules Verne (UPJV)]] gold medalist in 2008.<ref>[http://eetd.lbl.gov/dls/lecture-07-13-09-tarascon.html Distinguished Lecture Series: Jean-Marie Tarascon] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141219080401/http://eetd.lbl.gov/dls/lecture-07-13-09-tarascon.html |date=2014-12-19 }}, [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]]</ref> He won the [[ENI award|ENI Protection of the Environment award]] in 2011.<ref name=eni/> In 2015 he was awarded the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]'s [[Centenary Prize]].<ref name="RSCAP2015">{{cite web|url=http://www.rsc.org/news-events/rsc-news/articles/2015/may/awards-and-prizes-2015/|title=Royal Society of Chemistry Prizes and Awards 2015|publisher=[[Royal Society of Chemistry]]|accessdate=7 May 2015}}</ref> In 2016, he received an honorary doctorate '[[Doctor Honoris Causa|doctor honoris causa]]' from [[Hasselt University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Honorary doctorate recipients |url=https://www.uhasselt.be/en/about-hasselt-university/our-history/honorary-doctorate-recipients |access-date=2023-10-30 |website=UHasselt |language=en}}</ref> In 2017, he was one of the two winners of the Eric and Sheila Samson Prime Minister's Prize for Innovation in Alternative Fuels for Transportation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://fuelchoicessummit.com/Award.aspx|title=Fuel Choices and Smart Mobiity Summit > Award|last=Summit|first=Fuel Choices and Smart Mobiity|website=fuelchoicessummit.com|language=en-US|access-date=2018-03-16|archive-date=2018-03-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180308003624/http://www.fuelchoicessummit.com/Award.aspx|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was one of the five nominated for the CNRS Innovation Medals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cnrs.fr/en/research/awards/innovation.htm|title=CNRS - CNRS Innovation medalists|last=CNRS|website=www.cnrs.fr|language=fr|access-date=2018-03-16}}</ref> In 2020 he received the [[Balzan Prize]] for Environmental Challenges: Materials Science for Renewable Energy.<ref>[https://www.balzan.org/en/prizewinners/jean-marie-tarascon Balzan Prize 2020]</ref>
